items.title: Warframe of Mind: Chilling with the Iceblade of Narin update
From Narin to Tau, 'Warframe's Next Step
items.summary: ©INVENAt the recent 'Tenno VIP 2026 Seoul,' Digital Extremes clearly showed where 'Warframe' is heading next.
items.content:
Korean (한국어) KO Add us on ©INVEN At the recent 'Tenno VIP 2026 Seoul,' Digital Extremes clearly showed where 'Warframe' is heading next. From the Korean culture-inspired new Warframe 'Narin' to the 6-player cooperative challenge 'The Icebind,' and Tau, which had long existed only in lore—the big picture of where the game is headed was made abundantly clear.

However, not everything could be addressed on-site. Deeper topics—such as the design philosophy behind Narin, how the 6-player content differs from traditional 4-player missions, and what role Tau will play in Warframe's evolving story—could not be fully asked due to time constraints.

Following Tenno VIP 2026 Seoul, we sent several additional questions to Digital Extremes. Responding to us was Megan Everett, Community Director for Warframe. In this interview, centered on 'Iceblade of Narin,' we discussed the design direction for the new Warframe, the intentions behind 'The Icebind,' Warframe beyond Tau, and why the team has been actively highlighting the Korean community lately—delving deeper into stories that couldn't be fully covered on-site.

Narin is Warframe's first female Cold-themed Warframe. With Frost already serving as an iconic Cold Warframe, what was the most important consideration in crafting Narin's unique playstyle and identity?

Megan Everett: At Digital Extremes, we always love a good challenge. Creative Director Rebecca Ford originally had a personal goal to have a Warframe for every letter of the English alphabet. After reaching that goal, we started thinking about how we could diversify Warframes even further in fun ways.

Frost was released back in 2013 during Warframe's early days, and a very long time had passed before we revisited ice as a core theme. With Tau right on the horizon, it felt like the right moment to revisit this classic theme and create a special Warframe that complements Frost both aesthetically and gameplay-wise, while possessing a completely unique look and feel.

To achieve that, Narin's abilities and playstyle needed to be distinctly different from Frost's, while still grounding themselves in the existing mechanics of Cold elemental damage. Incorporating elements of sword dancing and skating allowed us to follow those Cold mechanics while giving Narin her own distinct identity in terms of mobility and overall gameplay feel.

Narin was designed to utilize the Cold Status Effect for both offense and defense, rather than just freezing enemies. In recent Warframe designs, are ability synergy and status effect utilization becoming even more important?

Megan Everett: Synergy is always important, though it's hard to say it's more crucial now than in the past. Above all, the thrill of discovery and fun must come first. Ability kits should remain open-ended so players can experiment with different loadouts and uncover playstyles that even we, as developers, didn't anticipate.

When combined with mods, weapons, armor sets, and other customization options, players can create builds so freely that they even surprise their own squadmates. We absolutely love seeing that happen in Warframe.

Narin heavily incorporates elements inspired by Korean culture. Beyond adopting superficial design motifs, what process did you go through to seamlessly integrate Korean imagery into the Warframe universe?

Megan Everett: Cultural inspiration is immensely important to everyone at Digital Extremes. We want to create content that diverse players can connect with in different ways. To do that, you can't just use a few colors or patterns. For something to truly resonate with people, you have to push yourself beyond the surface level across narrative, gameplay, character design, and many other aspects.

It's crucial that how deeply we care shows through in a meaningful way. It needs to be crafted with responsibility and love, and ultimately, it must always feel like it naturally belongs in the Warframe universe.

We draw inspiration from so many things—media, culture, history—the list is endless.

Protea Prime

A master of battlefield preparation, Protea Prime brings tactical ingenuity and devastating technology to every mission. Deploy her arsenal, control the flow of combat and keep your squad supplied while turning the battlefield to your advantage. Protea Prime is a versatile addition to any Arsenal, giving Tenno the tools to adapt to whatever the Origin System throws their way.

Ivara Prime

Stalking from the shadows and waiting for the perfect moment to strike, Ivara Prime is a huntress ready to claim her prey. Ivara Prime draws her bow and disappears into the shadows before striking with deadly precision. With a versatile Quiver, powerful Artemis Bow and the ability to move unseen, Ivara Prime is a natural choice for Tenno who prefer stealth and careful execution.

Prime Warframes

Want to learn more about Prime Warframes? Check out our Guide to Prime Warframes video for a helpful breakdown of what Prime Warframes are, different ways you can earn them and how you can purchase Prime items.

items.title: Warframe’s Halloween 2026 Events
items.summary: With Iceblade of Narin now live, there's lots to see and do at Yuvan Peak and elsewhere aboard the Zariman. But after you've had a chance to explore our latest update, the spooky season beckons… Move from the chilly to the chilling with a l
items.content:
With Iceblade of Narin now live, there's lots to see and do at Yuvan Peak and elsewhere aboard the Zariman. But after you've had a chance to explore our latest update, the spooky season beckons… Move from the chilly to the chilling with a look at Warframe's seasonal October content below:

Nights of Naberus

October 1 @ 11 a.m. ET - November 2 @ 11 a.m. ET Your favorite spine-tingling, seasonal event is back with a bevy of bone-chilling items available from Daughter in exchange for Mother Tokens. Alongside a full inventory of previous offerings, you'll also find some tempting new treats, including:
  • Calaverita Liset Skin
  • Follie Coulrophobia Glyph
  • Voruna Prime Massacre Glyph
  • Sirius vs. Orion Poster
As in years past, Mother Tokens can be obtained by completing Bounties in the Cambion Drift, or by trading additional Resources with Grandmother.

Hallowed Nightmares

October 1 @ 11 a.m. ET - November 2 @ 11 a.m. ET During the Nights of the Naberus, you'll have the opportunity to take on a Halloween-themed Tactical Alert not seen for several years. Face down the fearsome Jack O'Naut to earn the all-new Jack O’Naut Keychain Sugatra along with:
  • Jack O'Naut Recall Glyph
  • Manic Noggle
  • 50,000 Credits

"Scare-o" Ki'Teer Returns

October 16 @ 9 a.m. ET - November 8 @ 9 a.m. ET The Void Trader's vexing variant will once again make a series of weekend appearances all month long, offering his usual wares along with some beautifully baleful items you haven't seen before! If you enjoyed his unique inventory last time around, you won't want to miss what he's bringing to this year's bizarre bazaar starting at 9 a.m. ET and ending at 9 a.m. ET on the following dates:
  • Visit 1: October 16 - October 18
  • Visit 2: October 23 - October 25
  • Visit 3: October 30 - November 1
  • Visit 4: November 6 - November 8

Tennotober

October 1 @ 12:01 a.m. ET - October 31 @ 11:59 p.m. ET It wouldn't be fall without Tennotober, Warframe's community art challenge supporting the Princess Margaret Cancer Foundation Quest. Find this year's guidelines and prompts on the official Warframe Forums, where you can share your illustrations and Capturas to participate.

Excalibur Nights of Naberus Plushie Giveaway

October 1 @ 11 a.m. ET - October 9 @ 11 a.m. ET We've collaborated with our friends at Makeship to bring you a delightfully devilish new plushie version of Excalibur. Adorned with the Nyctalus Ephemera and colored for the occasion, the master swordsman looks markedly malevolent yet cuddly as ever. We're giving one away to three lucky Tenno who enter our giveaway via Gleam.

items.title: Iceblade of Narin Official Soundtrack
items.summary: Amid the frigid fanfare of our Iceblade of Narin launch, we're proud to once again deliver Warframe's latest musical tracks to major streaming platforms for your listening enjoyment. The talent, creativity and ingenuity of our remarkable So
items.content:
Amid the frigid fanfare of our Iceblade of Narin launch, we're proud to once again deliver Warframe's latest musical tracks to major streaming platforms for your listening enjoyment. The talent, creativity and ingenuity of our remarkable Sound Team reverberates across the three tracks comprising this release. Drawing inspiration from a traditional Korean musical style called Sanjo, each song evokes the powerful, dynamic movements of a sword dancer — just like our 66th Warframe, Narin. The melodies recorded for Neote's Dance also inspired the vocals in Ice Speaker, which further combines familiar tunes associated with both the Zariman and the Man in the Wall for a unique aural motif befitting the narrative strands threaded through our latest update (as well as the intensity of the upcoming Glacial Defiance game mode).

Where can I listen?

You can find the Iceblade of Narin Official Soundtrack on:

  • Apple Music
  • YouTube Music

items.title: Warframe: Banshee Prime Build and Post Rework Review
items.summary: Banshee's little rework in the most recent update in Warframe is very nice and makes her pretty viable in all forms of content in game.
items.content:
In the most recent update for Warframe, the Iceblade of Narin , one of the oldest warframes in the game, got a slight touch-up to her abilities. This streamlined her for more accessibility to what she can bring to the table. Banshee has always been in a weird spot, as players who know how to use her can make her dangerous, but most players (me included) didn’t understand her properly; this one touch-up made her easier to understand and, as such, gave her a new lease on life. So much so that I finally picked her back up and figured her out. Below will be our site’s recommended build for her in 2026.

Below is the build for her, which uses no forma, as I am using her Prime variant. If you are using the normal Banshee you got for free, simply copy what you see below with the forma you need to spend:

To get one thing out of the way quickly, I subsumed her 4th ability for Cyte-09’s Evade ability. This gives her invisibility to synergize with her other abilities so long as you keep getting headshot kills. From here, it’s pretty standard, just mostly build for a balance of each stack, with most of it going to range. Just make sure to add Arcane Crepuscular from the Hex’s shop in 1999.

Below are the Archon Shards I landed on for her. These are purely for flavor, and you can swap them out for whatever you wish.

As stated previously, the touch-up to her abilities is quite nice. You aren’t rooted in place, and everything feels much easier to understand with her abilities. I do respect the decision they made not to completely rework her kit. Especially if we look at past reworks like Oberon’s. But this little touch-up made me enjoy using her more. I would highly recommend using the Dual Torxica with this build. This is due to the fact that those pistols give lingering cold procs to random enemies, slowing them down so you can hit the weak points created with Sonar. It’s a killer build for Steel Path and beyond in Warframe.

items.title: Warframe: Nunchasa Build and Review
items.summary: The Nunchasa is a sleek, stylish and strong new bow in warframe. This article will be our recommended build and overall review of it!
items.content:
The Iceblade of Narin update has been filled with many misses, but that cannot be applied to the new weapons and Narin herself. Including the Nunchasa, a new Ice-focused bow that is just flat-out fun and great to use in all levels of content. It’s cool (pun intended), strong, and very stylish. Below will be our recommended build and review for it in Warframe!

Below will be our recommended build for the Nunchasa, which will need 3 formas altogether:

Nunchasa is a very critical-focused weapon, so a cocktail of the usual mods to play it into that goes well with how the weapon performs. I strongly encourage Hunter Munitions and Primary Deadhead to ensure each pull of the bow and aiming at the head pays off. Trust me, you will need it in higher levels of content.

I have practically zero complaints about the Nunchasa in Warframe . It’s the first bow in a long time with its own unique quirk that really needed a fire rate mod to enhance. When you get enough hits with it, you can let loose a special charged shot that deals very good damage to adds in a straight line. Not to mention it looks absolute sick to boot. I strongly encourage farming the Zariman for the Entropic Kuva to earn it; trust me.

Disclaimer – Digital Extremes provided Nunchasa for usage in this article.

items.title: Warframe: Narin Build and Review
items.summary: Narin is the latest new warframe in the game that can be a very strong weapons platform, with a horrible grind to earn her.
items.content:
Despite the overall Iceblade of Narin update being very contentious with the Warframe community, the titular frame, Narin, actually ended up being very enjoyable for the most part. Despite her ultimate being way too inconsistent, Narin herself can be a very strong solo-play weapons platform with the right build. Below will be our recommended build, followed by our review of her!

Below is our recommended build for her, Steel Path tested and only needing 2 formas to achieve:

To just go over the stats, stacking all your chips into range is best for Narin’s 3rd ability. Everything else boasts constant usage of abilities combined with Energy Nexus. Arcane Ice Storm is a must for her, as her abilities focus on freezing enemies as well.

Below will be our recommended Archon Shards for her; these are purely for flavor, and you can swap these out with whichever ones you prefer for her.

To address a pretty massive elephant in the room, it is hard to recommend the farm for her right now. Her blueprints are all tied to an already pretty bloated loot pool in the Zariman. If you have time to kill and don’t mind the Entropic Kuva farm, feel free to go after her. If you do not, wait to see if future hotfixes help alleviate the grind.

Now, as for the frame herself, her first 3 abilities take some getting used to. However, when you get into the rhythm with her, she can be a very excellent warframe to take into high-level content, if only because of how her third ability boosts damage against enemies with your weapons. However, I recommend removing her 4th ability, as it is wildly inconsistent to use. When it is working, its keeping adds cleared very well. But sometimes you can get stuck aiming at an enemy that can’t take damage from it, like the fragmented triangle enemy that needs to be hit in the arms to kill. Or enemies in nullifier bubbles that waste the charge. I recommend using Nourish or any armor-stripping ability.

Disclaimer – Digital Extremes provided Narin for usage in this article.

As per the latest hotfix deployed by Digital Extremes, all problems stated above with Narin’s ultimate ability have been fixed. Below is a new build that properly stacks power strength to get the most out of it in all levels of content. I just wish the ultimate did not need a full charge to use a single blast if you just need a crowd cleared out.

Diaries is about to have its 'biggest year yet' 27 years later, EverQuest Legends is just getting started In late 2026, Warframe will take players to Tau, an entirely new solar system. But in what has become the norm for the long-running multiplayer game, creative director Rebecca Ford is looking backward and forward at the same time.

“The impossible task of anyone working on Warframe is choosing when to go new or choosing when to revisit,” Ford told Polygon on a recent call. The team is laying groundwork for Tau at a breakneck pace. Warframe ’s fall update, The Iceblade of Narin will introduce a new Warframe and in-game hub on Sept. 23.

Then, on Oct. 15 a special event called Epoch Operation: Tau will launch, which is something that I will show to people who don’t know much about Warframe so that I can witness their bafflement (it involves piloting a skyscraper-sized spaceship that looks like a large nude humanoid).

As if that weren’t enough, the team is also launching a new six-player cooperative game mode called Glacial Defiance, which is definitely not a raid.

“We had raids. They lived, they died, they're gone,” said Ford. “We are auditioning for a role of six-player, slightly demanding gameplay. Do you show up?”

Warframe ’s raids, officially known as Trials, were retired in 2018. At the time, design director Pablo Alonso explained that maintaining the game mode was a massive effort and timesink for the dev team — and that not enough players were actually engaging with it. Those who did though, seem to be diehards.

“There are players that know the old Warframe raids that stay around and talk about them to this day,” Ford said. Warframe has also become the de facto home for refugees from Destiny and Destiny 2 . In Warframe they’re finding cool weapons, zippy gameplay, and probably less toxicity. But the challenge the Warframe devs face is, ironically, a lack of challenge. High-level players with a mind for synergy can sweep through missions in a matter of minutes, carrying lesser ones to the finish line on a wave of neon explosions.

Image: Digital Extremes Is this awesome? Absolutely. But there is presumably a growing contingent of people who want their dopamine rush served with a side of strategic teamwork.

“The selfish tangent to this, which is both incriminating and honest, is I have a group of friends I play Deadlock with and we lament that there's nothing for us to do in Warframe because we have to leave two people out all the time,” Ford said. “So we'll see — is there a social niche for this? Are there groups of six players that want to do some Warframe stuff together that can't right now? And the answer to all those questions will be who knows, please be patient with us.”

In the two years that I’ve been playing Warframe , Digital Extremes has introduced multiple new Warframes, story quests, and now a solar system. In that same time, they have redone facial animations that date back to 2015, and periodically revamp older Warframes to bring their kits in line with the game’s modern, free-flowing gameplay. Not all the changes have been well-received in the moment: A horror mode called Follie’s Hunt proved destabilizing for a player community used to melting enemies with ease.

Image: Digital Extremes “I would say that was one of the low points of the year so far, which is great, which means we've only gone up since then,” said Ford.

Another adds more missions for the Railjack, a spaceship whose dogfight gameplay has been divisive. Revisiting it, said Ford, was “a dangerous thing for any Warframe dev to do.” Every change is a gamble — but a bold necessity — in a live-service game.

“The harshest reality check is when people disagree with your definition of fun for what I would call ‘our game,’ but the community would say, ‘No, no, this is actually our game, you make it for us,’” Ford said, laughing. “And we're like, ‘Damn, they got us again!’ Any developer who accidentally or intentionally makes a live service game must experience the ritual or the witchcraft that separates the self from the service. You always wish you had more time. You always wish you had more resources, but you need to deliver something.”
